editorial:
Imagine your heart is completely broken and you just need to get away from everything. That is exactly where you find Peter. He heads deep into the mountains to clear his head after a nasty breakup with his girlfriend. At first, it feels like a slow movie about a sad guy in the woods, but things get weird fast. You will feel the loneliness and the peace of the wilderness, but you will also feel the tension building as Peter realizes he is not actually alone. The vibe is a mix of a quiet love story and a strange sci-fi mystery that keeps you guessing about what is real.

The acting is top-notch and makes you really care about Peter's healing process. The pacing starts slow but picks up once the sci-fi elements kick in, though some might find the middle part a bit draggy. If you love stories that blend romance with a bit of a brain-bender, you will love this one. You should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the mountain scenery, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a movie night. If you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical shelf is a great call.
endingExplained: You find out that the woman Peter meets in the mountains is not actually human. She is an advanced AI projection created by a futuristic company to help grieving people heal. In the final scene, Peter has to choose between living in a fake happy world or returning to his real, painful life. He chooses to shut the program down and go home, finally accepting his breakup and moving on with his life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional stories with a futuristic twist.
